1: # Windows hooks (implemented). The contract every mk/os/<os>.mk provides:
2: #
3: #   EXE                    executable suffix
4: #   TARGET_TRIPLE          the cargo target triple
5: #   KERNEL_BUILD           build the kernel leaf
6: #   KERNEL_TEST            run the kernel leaf's op tests (GPU)
7: #   KERNEL_BUILD_INPUTS    extra files whose change makes a CUDA server stale
8: #   GPU_STATUS             print VRAM use and the processes that may hold it
9: #   GPU_GUARD              exit non-zero while the GPU is held
10: #   GPU_PROFILE            run the explicit GPU test profile
11: #   SERVER_START           start $(SERVER_BIN) in the background, wait for ready
12: #   SERVER_STOP            stop it (FORCE=1: any ignis-server)
13: #   SERVER_STATUS          report the background server process
14: #   DEV_UI                 server + Vite as one foreground session; Ctrl+C
15: #                          (or the session dying) stops both
16: #   OS_REQUIRED_TOOLS      tools `make doctor` requires
17: #   OS_OPTIONAL_TOOLS      tools `make doctor` only reports
18: #   OS_TOOL_HINT           where those tools come from
19: #   OS_DOCTOR              extra `make doctor` checks (sh, ending in `;`)
20: 
21: # GNU make on Windows falls back to cmd.exe when it finds no sh.exe on PATH;
22: # every recipe here is POSIX sh.
23: ifeq ($(findstring sh,$(notdir $(SHELL))),)
24:   $(error no POSIX sh found (SHELL=$(SHELL)): install Git for Windows and put its usr\bin on PATH)
25: endif
26: 
27: EXE := .exe
28: TARGET_TRIPLE ?= x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
29: 
30: # `exec` is load-bearing. GNU make for Windows (the Chocolatey build is 32-bit)
31: # runs a metacharacter-free command line itself, and a 32-bit parent resolves
32: # `powershell` to the SysWOW64 copy: a 32-bit PowerShell that cannot see
33: # System32\nvidia-smi.exe, so every GPU check fails. A shell builtin makes make
34: # hand the line to sh (64-bit), which starts the real 64-bit PowerShell. Since
35: # `exec` replaces the shell, a $(PS) hook must be the last command on its line.
36: PS := exec powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
37: 
38: KERNEL_BUILD = $(PS) -File kernel/build.ps1
39: KERNEL_TEST = $(PS) -File kernel/build.ps1 build -Test
40: KERNEL_BUILD_INPUTS := $(wildcard kernel/build.ps1)
41: 
42: GPU_STATUS = $(PS) -File mk/windows/gpu.ps1 -Action status
43: GPU_GUARD = $(PS) -File mk/windows/gpu.ps1 -Action guard -ThresholdMiB $(GPU_THRESHOLD_MIB)
44: GPU_PROFILE = $(PS) -File scripts/gpu-profile.ps1 $(GPU_PROFILE_ARGS)
45: 
46: # server.ps1 reads its inputs from the environment: the flag string passes
47: # through sh and PowerShell untouched that way.

1: // The chat request the Playground sends (GitHub #164): ignis's own
2: // `POST /v1/chat/completions`, streaming with the usage chunk, plus the
3: // thinking effort and the ignis lane tag extension `class`. With tools on,
4: // it also declares them, and the system message is the ignis prompt (what
5: // the tools add, read-only) followed by the owner's own.
6: 
7: import type { ToolCall } from "./sse.ts";
8: 
9: export type LaneTag = "interactive" | "agent";
10: 
11: /**
12:  * The efforts the loaded Qwen 3.8 template accepts (`high` is refused).
13:  * `none` turns thinking off, so the request never also sends
14:  * `enable_thinking` — ignis rejects the two when they disagree.
15:  */
16: export const REASONING_EFFORTS = ["none", "low", "medium", "xhigh"] as const;
17: export type ReasoningEffort = (typeof REASONING_EFFORTS)[number];
18: 
19: export type Settings = {
20:   model: string;
21:   systemPrompt: string;
22:   temperature: number;
23:   topP: number;
24:   /** `null` leaves the cap to the engine. */
25:   maxTokens: number | null;
26:   reasoningEffort: ReasoningEffort;
27:   laneTag: LaneTag;
28: };
29: 
30: /** A turn of the conversation: an assistant turn may call tools, a tool turn answers one call. */
31: export type Turn = { role: "user" | "assistant" | "tool"; content: string; toolCalls?: ToolCall[]; toolCallId?: string };
32: 
33: /** An OpenAI function tool, as `tools[]` declares it. */
34: export type ToolDefinition = {
35:   type: "function";
36:   function: { name: string; description: string; parameters: object };
37: };
38: 
39: type WireMessage = {
40:   role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool";
41:   content: string;
42:   tool_calls?: { id: string; type: "function"; function: { name: string; arguments: string } }[];
43:   tool_call_id?: string;
44: };
45: 
46: export type ChatRequest = {
47:   model: string;
48:   messages: WireMessage[];
49:   tools?: ToolDefinition[];
50:   stream: true;
51:   stream_options: { include_usage: true };
52:   temperature: number;
53:   top_p: number;
54:   max_tokens?: number;
55:   reasoning_effort: ReasoningEffort;
56:   class: LaneTag;
57: };
58: 
59: /** One message already in the Playground's conversation. */
60: export type Exchange = Turn & { failed: boolean };
61: 
62: /**
63:  * What of the conversation goes back to the engine: every exchange except
64:  * the ones that produced nothing — a prompt whose reply failed or came back
65:  * empty is dropped together with that reply, so the history never holds two
66:  * user turns in a row. A reply stopped part-way keeps the text it got.
67:  * Reasoning is never resent.
68:  */
69: export function conversationTurns(entries: Exchange[]): Turn[] {
70:   const turns: Turn[] = [];
71:   // A reply that only called tools is not empty: its calls are the turn.
72:   const empty = (e: Exchange | undefined) =>
73:     e !== undefined && e.role === "assistant" && (e.failed || (!e.content && !e.toolCalls?.length));
74:   for (let i = 0; i < entries.length; i++) {
75:     const entry = entries[i];
76:     if (entry.role === "user" && empty(entries[i + 1])) {
77:       i++;
78:       continue;
79:     }
80:     if (empty(entry)) continue;
81:     turns.push({
82:       role: entry.role,
83:       content: entry.content,
84:       ...(entry.toolCalls?.length ? { toolCalls: entry.toolCalls } : {}),
85:       ...(entry.toolCallId ? { toolCallId: entry.toolCallId } : {}),
86:     });
87:   }
88:   return turns;
89: }
90: 
91: function wireMessage(turn: Turn): WireMessage {
92:   return {
93:     role: turn.role,
94:     content: turn.content,
95:     ...(turn.toolCalls?.length
96:       ? {
97:           tool_calls: turn.toolCalls.map((c) => ({
98:             id: c.id,
99:             type: "function" as const,
100:             function: { name: c.name, arguments: c.arguments },
101:           })),
102:         }
103:       : {}),
104:     ...(turn.toolCallId ? { tool_call_id: turn.toolCallId } : {}),
105:   };
106: }
107: 
108: /** What the enabled tools add to a request: their prompt, ahead of the owner's, and their definitions. */
109: export type ToolExtras = { ignisPrompt?: string; tools?: ToolDefinition[] };
110: 
111: export function buildChatRequest(settings: Settings, turns: Turn[], extras: ToolExtras = {}): ChatRequest {
112:   const system = [extras.ignisPrompt ?? "", settings.systemPrompt].filter((part) => part.trim() !== "").join("\n\n");
113:   return {
114:     model: settings.model,
115:     messages: [...(system ? [{ role: "system" as const, content: system }] : []), ...turns.map(wireMessage)],
116:     ...(extras.tools?.length ? { tools: extras.tools } : {}),
117:     stream: true,
118:     stream_options: { include_usage: true },
119:     temperature: settings.temperature,
120:     top_p: settings.topP,
121:     ...(settings.maxTokens !== null ? { max_tokens: settings.maxTokens } : {}),
122:     reasoning_effort: settings.reasoningEffort,
123:     class: settings.laneTag,
124:   };
125: }

Issues live **exclusively on GitHub** (`gpillon/ignis`, via the `gh` CLI).
GitHub is the single source of truth for issue tracking: status, blocking
relationships, labels, and closure. Each GitHub issue body is short
(1-3 lines of context) and links to the implementation spec.

Implementation specs (acceptance criteria, seam description, ADR references)
live under `.scratch/<feature>/specs/` in this repo. These are **specs, not

(`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`).

experiments, start from `docs/findings/README.md`.

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal
until Ctrl+C. `run` and `start` only ever launch the last build: a stale
binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

1: # ignis kernel leaf: C++/CUDA static libraries behind a flat C ABI (ADR 0001),
2: # built on a vendored subtree of the reference's core and ops (ADR 0010).
3: # See kernel/NOTICE and kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md for provenance.
4: #
5: # Configure/build: kernel/build.ps1 (plain PowerShell, imports the MSVC env
6: # itself — same pattern as ninfer's configure-ninja.ps1/build-ninja.ps1).
7: # Run the leaf's own tests: kernel/build.ps1 -Test (or ctest from the build
8: # directory).
9: 
10: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
11: project(ignis-kernel LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)
12: 
13: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
15: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)
16: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
17: 
18: # RTX 5090 (Blackwell consumer). Proven on this machine with CMake 3.28
19: # (NINFER_WINDOWS_BUILD_NOTES section 14).
20: if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)
21:   set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 120a)
22: endif()
23: 
24: # -GS- : the kernel objects are linked into a Rust binary via lld, which cannot
25: # satisfy the /GS security-cookie symbols (__security_cookie,
26: # __security_check_cookie, __GSHandlerCheck) that MSVC emits by default. /GS is
27: # irrelevant for compute kernels (no stack-buffer semantics), so disable it —
28: # for the C++ translation units of the vendored core as well as for CUDA. The
29: # final Rust link provides the MSVC CRT (build.rs).
30: set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler -GS-")
31: set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} /GS-")
32: 
33: # CUDA::cudart (P1-07, GitHub #43; also needed by P1-08, GitHub #44; also
34: # needed by the P1-10/#46 bf16/w8 dispatch below, and by P1-16/#52's
35: # paged_kv_cache/linear_attention_state, which pull cudaStream_t in through
36: # core/device.h): the vendored op wrappers' public headers declare
37: # host-callable functions taking a `cudaStream_t`, and the op-test harness
38: # calls the CUDA runtime API (cudaMemcpyAsync, stream sync) directly from
39: # plain .cpp translation units — unlike the .cu sources, MSVC's cl.exe does
40: # not see the CUDA toolkit's include/lib dirs on its own for those.
41: find_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)
42: 
43: # --- the vendored reference substrate (ADR 0010, GitHub #42, #43, #44, #46, #52) -
44: #
45: # Verbatim copies of the reference's core, ops-common headers and (from P1-07)
46: # the norm/glue op families, pinned by kernel/vendor/manifest.json and
47: # maintained by scripts/vendor-ninfer.ps1. Vendored files keep the reference's
48: # include paths (`core/...`, `ops/common/...`, `ops/kernel/...`,
49: # `ops/launcher/...`), so `kernel/vendor/src` is the include root and a diff
50: # against the source stays trivial. Public op headers keep the reference's
51: # `ninfer/ops/...` include path, rooted at `kernel/vendor/include`.
52: #
53: # The source list is explicit, not a glob: the manifest is the only thing that
54: # decides what is vendored, and a glob would silently absorb a stray file.
55: set(IGNIS_VENDOR_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/vendor)
56: add_library(ignis_vendor STATIC

67:   ${IGNIS_VENDOR_DIR}/src/ops/launcher/embed_gather.cu

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal
until Ctrl+C. `run` and `start` only ever launch the last build: a stale
binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in

diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal

binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

1: # ignis kernel leaf: C++/CUDA static libraries behind a flat C ABI (ADR 0001),
2: # built on a vendored subtree of the reference's core and ops (ADR 0010).
3: # See kernel/NOTICE and kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md for provenance.
4: #
5: # Configure/build: kernel/build.ps1 (plain PowerShell, imports the MSVC env
6: # itself — same pattern as ninfer's configure-ninja.ps1/build-ninja.ps1).
7: # Run the leaf's own tests: kernel/build.ps1 -Test (or ctest from the build
8: # directory).
9: 
10: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
11: project(ignis-kernel LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)
12: 
13: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
15: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)
16: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
17: 
18: # RTX 5090 (Blackwell consumer). Proven on this machine with CMake 3.28
19: # (NINFER_WINDOWS_BUILD_NOTES section 14).
20: if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)
21:   set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 120a)
22: endif()
23: 
24: # -GS- : the kernel objects are linked into a Rust binary via lld, which cannot
25: # satisfy the /GS security-cookie symbols (__security_cookie,
26: # __security_check_cookie, __GSHandlerCheck) that MSVC emits by default. /GS is
27: # irrelevant for compute kernels (no stack-buffer semantics), so disable it —
28: # for the C++ translation units of the vendored core as well as for CUDA. The
29: # final Rust link provides the MSVC CRT (build.rs).
30: set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler -GS-")
31: set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} /GS-")
32: 
33: # CUDA::cudart (P1-07, GitHub #43; also needed by P1-08, GitHub #44; also
34: # needed by the P1-10/#46 bf16/w8 dispatch below, and by P1-16/#52's
35: # paged_kv_cache/linear_attention_state, which pull cudaStream_t in through
36: # core/device.h): the vendored op wrappers' public headers declare
37: # host-callable functions taking a `cudaStream_t`, and the op-test harness
38: # calls the CUDA runtime API (cudaMemcpyAsync, stream sync) directly from
39: # plain .cpp translation units — unlike the .cu sources, MSVC's cl.exe does
40: # not see the CUDA toolkit's include/lib dirs on its own for those.
41: find_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)
42: 
43: # --- the vendored reference substrate (ADR 0010, GitHub #42, #43, #44, #46, #52) -
44: #
45: # Verbatim copies of the reference's core, ops-common headers and (from P1-07)
46: # the norm/glue op families, pinned by kernel/vendor/manifest.json and
47: # maintained by scripts/vendor-ninfer.ps1. Vendored files keep the reference's
48: # include paths (`core/...`, `ops/common/...`, `ops/kernel/...`,
49: # `ops/launcher/...`), so `kernel/vendor/src` is the include root and a diff
50: # against the source stays trivial. Public op headers keep the reference's
51: # `ninfer/ops/...` include path, rooted at `kernel/vendor/include`.
52: #
53: # The source list is explicit, not a glob: the manifest is the only thing that
54: # decides what is vendored, and a glob would silently absorb a stray file.
55: set(IGNIS_VENDOR_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/vendor)

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live **exclusively on GitHub** (`gpillon/ignis`, via the `gh` CLI).
GitHub is the single source of truth for issue tracking: status, blocking
relationships, labels, and closure. Each GitHub issue body is short
(1-3 lines of context) and links to the implementation spec.

Implementation specs (acceptance criteria, seam description, ADR references)
live under `.scratch/<feature>/specs/` in this repo. These are **specs, not
issues** — they do not track status or blocking (that is GitHub's job).
`.scratch/` is also used for temporary artifacts, experiments, and workflow
output, but **never for issue tracking**.

See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for the full convention.

### Triage labels

The five canonical triage roles, mapped 1:1 to same-name labels
(`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`).
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context — root `CONTEXT.md` for the glossary, `docs/adr/` for ADRs.
See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Findings

When recording or consulting durable findings from discovery, research, or
experiments, start from `docs/findings/README.md`.

### Testing

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

### Make

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal
until Ctrl+C. `run` and `start` only ever launch the last build: a stale
binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

### Worktrees

All git worktrees for this repo live under `../.inference-qwen-worktrees/`
(sibling of the repo root), one subdirectory per issue/feature. Do not create
worktrees anywhere else (e.g. no separate `.inference-claude-worktrees/`) —
one shared location for every agent.

2: #
3: #   make                 the target list (same as `make help`)
4: #   make dev             build ignis-server, then run it (GPU, release, Playground)
5: #   make run             run the last build; refuses a missing or stale binary
6: #   make mock            the same loop on the CPU mock (no GPU, no kernel leaf)
7: #   make dev-ui          server in the background + Playground with hot reload
8: #                        (API_KEY=auto: the server generates a key and prints it;
9: #                        EXPOSE=cloudflare-quick: a public URL, key required)
10: #   make config          the resolved knobs
11: #
12: # Layout
13: #   Makefile             the platform-neutral target graph (this file)
14: #   mk/config.mk         the knobs and their defaults (CUDA, PROFILE, UI, ...)
15: #   mk/os/<os>.mk        the per-OS hooks: target triple, kernel build, GPU
16: #                        checks, background server control. Windows is
17: #                        implemented; Linux is scaffolded and every hook it
18: #                        cannot run yet fails with a "not implemented" message.
19: #   mk/windows/*.ps1     the PowerShell helpers behind the Windows hooks
20: #   local.mk             untracked per-machine overrides (see local.mk.example)
21: #
22: # Precedence: command line > environment > local.mk > mk/config.mk.
23: #
24: # Recipes run under a POSIX sh: /bin/sh on Linux, Git for Windows' sh.exe on
25: # Windows (GNU make takes it from PATH). Keep them to plain sh + the tools
26: # listed by `make doctor`.
27: #
28: # There is deliberately no `fmt` target: the repo is not rustfmt-clean and
29: # diffs stay semantic-only.
30: 
31: MAKEFLAGS += --no-builtin-rules --no-builtin-variables
32: .SUFFIXES:
33: .DEFAULT_GOAL := help
34: # cargo, ninja and vite parallelize internally; make itself stays serial so a
35: # `run` never races its own freshness check or the GPU guard.

37: 
38: -include local.mk
39: include mk/config.mk

41: ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)

71: CARGO_TARGET := --target $(TARGET_TRIPLE)
72: SERVER_CARGO_FLAGS := -p ignis-server $(CARGO_TARGET) --profile $(PROFILE) $(if $(filter 1,$(CUDA)),--features cuda)
73: WORKSPACE_FEATURES := $(if $(filter 1,$(CUDA)),--features ignis-server/cuda)

80: BUILT_BACKEND = $(strip $(if $(wildcard $(SERVER_STAMP)),$(file < $(SERVER_STAMP))))

82: SERVER_URL := http://$(BIND)

1: // The chat request the Playground sends (GitHub #164): ignis's own
2: // `POST /v1/chat/completions`, streaming with the usage chunk, plus the
3: // thinking effort and the ignis lane tag extension `class`. With tools on,
4: // it also declares them, and the system message is the ignis prompt (what
5: // the tools add, read-only) followed by the owner's own.
6: 
7: import type { ToolCall } from "./sse.ts";
8: 
9: export type LaneTag = "interactive" | "agent";
10: 
11: /**
12:  * The efforts the loaded Qwen 3.8 template accepts (`high` is refused).
13:  * `none` turns thinking off, so the request never also sends
14:  * `enable_thinking` — ignis rejects the two when they disagree.
15:  */
16: export const REASONING_EFFORTS = ["none", "low", "medium", "xhigh"] as const;
17: export type ReasoningEffort = (typeof REASONING_EFFORTS)[number];
18: 
19: export type Settings = {
20:   model: string;
21:   systemPrompt: string;
22:   temperature: number;
23:   topP: number;
24:   /** `null` leaves the cap to the engine. */
25:   maxTokens: number | null;
26:   reasoningEffort: ReasoningEffort;
27:   laneTag: LaneTag;
28: };
29: 
30: /** A turn of the conversation: an assistant turn may call tools, a tool turn answers one call. */
31: export type Turn = { role: "user" | "assistant" | "tool"; content: string; toolCalls?: ToolCall[]; toolCallId?: string };
32: 
33: /** An OpenAI function tool, as `tools[]` declares it. */
34: export type ToolDefinition = {
35:   type: "function";
36:   function: { name: string; description: string; parameters: object };
37: };
38: 
39: type WireMessage = {
40:   role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool";
41:   content: string;
42:   tool_calls?: { id: string; type: "function"; function: { name: string; arguments: string } }[];
43:   tool_call_id?: string;
44: };
45: 
46: export type ChatRequest = {
47:   model: string;
48:   messages: WireMessage[];
49:   tools?: ToolDefinition[];
50:   stream: true;
51:   stream_options: { include_usage: true };
52:   temperature: number;
53:   top_p: number;
54:   max_tokens?: number;
55:   reasoning_effort: ReasoningEffort;
56:   class: LaneTag;
57: };
58: 
59: /** One message already in the Playground's conversation. */
60: export type Exchange = Turn & { failed: boolean };
61: 
62: /**
63:  * What of the conversation goes back to the engine: every exchange except
64:  * the ones that produced nothing — a prompt whose reply failed or came back
65:  * empty is dropped together with that reply, so the history never holds two
66:  * user turns in a row. A reply stopped part-way keeps the text it got.
67:  * Reasoning is never resent.
68:  */
69: export function conversationTurns(entries: Exchange[]): Turn[] {
70:   const turns: Turn[] = [];
71:   // A reply that only called tools is not empty: its calls are the turn.
72:   const empty = (e: Exchange | undefined) =>
73:     e !== undefined && e.role === "assistant" && (e.failed || (!e.content && !e.toolCalls?.length));
74:   for (let i = 0; i < entries.length; i++) {
75:     const entry = entries[i];
76:     if (entry.role === "user" && empty(entries[i + 1])) {
77:       i++;
78:       continue;
79:     }
80:     if (empty(entry)) continue;
81:     turns.push({
82:       role: entry.role,
83:       content: entry.content,
84:       ...(entry.toolCalls?.length ? { toolCalls: entry.toolCalls } : {}),
85:       ...(entry.toolCallId ? { toolCallId: entry.toolCallId } : {}),
86:     });
87:   }
88:   return turns;
89: }
90: 
91: function wireMessage(turn: Turn): WireMessage {
92:   return {
93:     role: turn.role,
94:     content: turn.content,
95:     ...(turn.toolCalls?.length
96:       ? {
97:           tool_calls: turn.toolCalls.map((c) => ({
98:             id: c.id,
99:             type: "function" as const,
100:             function: { name: c.name, arguments: c.arguments },
101:           })),
102:         }
103:       : {}),
104:     ...(turn.toolCallId ? { tool_call_id: turn.toolCallId } : {}),
105:   };
106: }
107: 
108: /** What the enabled tools add to a request: their prompt, ahead of the owner's, and their definitions. */
109: export type ToolExtras = { ignisPrompt?: string; tools?: ToolDefinition[] };
110: 
111: export function buildChatRequest(settings: Settings, turns: Turn[], extras: ToolExtras = {}): ChatRequest {
112:   const system = [extras.ignisPrompt ?? "", settings.systemPrompt].filter((part) => part.trim() !== "").join("\n\n");
113:   return {
114:     model: settings.model,
115:     messages: [...(system ? [{ role: "system" as const, content: system }] : []), ...turns.map(wireMessage)],
116:     ...(extras.tools?.length ? { tools: extras.tools } : {}),
117:     stream: true,
118:     stream_options: { include_usage: true },
119:     temperature: settings.temperature,
120:     top_p: settings.topP,
121:     ...(settings.maxTokens !== null ? { max_tokens: settings.maxTokens } : {}),
122:     reasoning_effort: settings.reasoningEffort,
123:     class: settings.laneTag,
124:   };
125: }

diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then

binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

1: # ignis kernel leaf: C++/CUDA static libraries behind a flat C ABI (ADR 0001),
2: # built on a vendored subtree of the reference's core and ops (ADR 0010).
3: # See kernel/NOTICE and kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md for provenance.
4: #
5: # Configure/build: kernel/build.ps1 (plain PowerShell, imports the MSVC env
6: # itself — same pattern as ninfer's configure-ninja.ps1/build-ninja.ps1).
7: # Run the leaf's own tests: kernel/build.ps1 -Test (or ctest from the build
8: # directory).
9: 
10: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
11: project(ignis-kernel LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)
12: 
13: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
15: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)
16: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
17: 
18: # RTX 5090 (Blackwell consumer). Proven on this machine with CMake 3.28
19: # (NINFER_WINDOWS_BUILD_NOTES section 14).
20: if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)
21:   set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 120a)
22: endif()
23: 
24: # -GS- : the kernel objects are linked into a Rust binary via lld, which cannot
25: # satisfy the /GS security-cookie symbols (__security_cookie,
26: # __security_check_cookie, __GSHandlerCheck) that MSVC emits by default. /GS is
27: # irrelevant for compute kernels (no stack-buffer semantics), so disable it —
28: # for the C++ translation units of the vendored core as well as for CUDA. The
29: # final Rust link provides the MSVC CRT (build.rs).
30: set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler -GS-")
31: set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} /GS-")
32: 
33: # CUDA::cudart (P1-07, GitHub #43; also needed by P1-08, GitHub #44; also
34: # needed by the P1-10/#46 bf16/w8 dispatch below, and by P1-16/#52's
35: # paged_kv_cache/linear_attention_state, which pull cudaStream_t in through
36: # core/device.h): the vendored op wrappers' public headers declare
37: # host-callable functions taking a `cudaStream_t`, and the op-test harness
38: # calls the CUDA runtime API (cudaMemcpyAsync, stream sync) directly from
39: # plain .cpp translation units — unlike the .cu sources, MSVC's cl.exe does
40: # not see the CUDA toolkit's include/lib dirs on its own for those.
41: find_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)
42: 
43: # --- the vendored reference substrate (ADR 0010, GitHub #42, #43, #44, #46, #52) -
44: #
45: # Verbatim copies of the reference's core, ops-common headers and (from P1-07)
46: # the norm/glue op families, pinned by kernel/vendor/manifest.json and
47: # maintained by scripts/vendor-ninfer.ps1. Vendored files keep the reference's
48: # include paths (`core/...`, `ops/common/...`, `ops/kernel/...`,
49: # `ops/launcher/...`), so `kernel/vendor/src` is the include root and a diff
50: # against the source stays trivial. Public op headers keep the reference's
51: # `ninfer/ops/...` include path, rooted at `kernel/vendor/include`.
52: #
53: # The source list is explicit, not a glob: the manifest is the only thing that
54: # decides what is vendored, and a glob would silently absorb a stray file.

# AGENTS.md

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live **exclusively on GitHub** (`gpillon/ignis`, via the `gh` CLI).
GitHub is the single source of truth for issue tracking: status, blocking
relationships, labels, and closure. Each GitHub issue body is short
(1-3 lines of context) and links to the implementation spec.

Implementation specs (acceptance criteria, seam description, ADR references)
live under `.scratch/<feature>/specs/` in this repo. These are **specs, not
issues** — they do not track status or blocking (that is GitHub's job).
`.scratch/` is also used for temporary artifacts, experiments, and workflow
output, but **never for issue tracking**.

See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for the full convention.

### Triage labels

The five canonical triage roles, mapped 1:1 to same-name labels
(`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`).
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context — root `CONTEXT.md` for the glossary, `docs/adr/` for ADRs.
See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Findings

When recording or consulting durable findings from discovery, research, or
experiments, start from `docs/findings/README.md`.

### Testing

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

2: #
3: #   make                 the target list (same as `make help`)
4: #   make dev             build ignis-server, then run it (GPU, release, Playground)
5: #   make run             run the last build; refuses a missing or stale binary
6: #   make mock            the same loop on the CPU mock (no GPU, no kernel leaf)
7: #   make dev-ui          server in the background + Playground with hot reload
8: #                        (API_KEY=auto: the server generates a key and prints it;
9: #                        EXPOSE=cloudflare-quick: a public URL, key required)
10: #   make config          the resolved knobs
11: #
12: # Layout
13: #   Makefile             the platform-neutral target graph (this file)
14: #   mk/config.mk         the knobs and their defaults (CUDA, PROFILE, UI, ...)
15: #   mk/os/<os>.mk        the per-OS hooks: target triple, kernel build, GPU
16: #                        checks, background server control. Windows is
17: #                        implemented; Linux is scaffolded and every hook it
18: #                        cannot run yet fails with a "not implemented" message.
19: #   mk/windows/*.ps1     the PowerShell helpers behind the Windows hooks
20: #   local.mk             untracked per-machine overrides (see local.mk.example)
21: #
22: # Precedence: command line > environment > local.mk > mk/config.mk.
23: #
24: # Recipes run under a POSIX sh: /bin/sh on Linux, Git for Windows' sh.exe on
25: # Windows (GNU make takes it from PATH). Keep them to plain sh + the tools
26: # listed by `make doctor`.
27: #
28: # There is deliberately no `fmt` target: the repo is not rustfmt-clean and
29: # diffs stay semantic-only.
30: 
31: MAKEFLAGS += --no-builtin-rules --no-builtin-variables
32: .SUFFIXES:
33: .DEFAULT_GOAL := help
34: # cargo, ninja and vite parallelize internally; make itself stays serial so a
35: # `run` never races its own freshness check or the GPU guard.

37: 
38: -include local.mk

41: ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)

76: SERVER_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/ignis-server$(EXE)
77: # Records the backend of the last `make build`, so `make run CUDA=1` cannot
78: # silently start a binary that was built as the CPU mock (or the reverse).
79: SERVER_STAMP := $(BIN_DIR)/ignis-server.backend
80: BUILT_BACKEND = $(strip $(if $(wildcard $(SERVER_STAMP)),$(file < $(SERVER_STAMP))))
81: 
82: SERVER_URL := http://$(BIND)
83: # The server's own default when METRICS_BIND is empty (DEFAULT_METRICS_BIND).
84: METRICS_URL := http://$(or $(METRICS_BIND),127.0.0.1:9464)
85: SERVER_PID := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ignis-server.pid
86: SERVER_LOG := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ignis-server.log
87: 
88: GPU_ENGINE_FLAGS = $(if $(ARTIFACT),--artifact $(ARTIFACT)) \
89:   $(if $(KV_FORMAT),--kv-format $(KV_FORMAT)) \
90:   $(if $(MAX_CONTEXT),--max-context $(MAX_CONTEXT)) \
91:   $(if $(PREFILL_CHUNK),--prefill-chunk $(PREFILL_CHUNK)) \
92:   $(if $(KV_POOL_BYTES),--kv-pool-bytes $(KV_POOL_BYTES)) \
93:   $(if $(KV_HOST_POOL_BYTES),--kv-host-pool-bytes $(KV_HOST_POOL_BYTES)) \
94:   $(if $(REQUEST_TIMEOUT),--request-timeout $(REQUEST_TIMEOUT)) \
95:   $(if $(SPEC),--spec $(SPEC) $(if $(DRAFT_TOKENS),--draft-tokens $(DRAFT_TOKENS)))
96: SERVER_FLAGS = --bind $(BIND) \
97:   $(if $(filter 1,$(CUDA)),$(GPU_ENGINE_FLAGS)) \
98:   $(if $(MODEL),--model $(MODEL)) \
99:   $(if $(filter 1,$(UI)),--ui) \
100:   $(if $(filter 1,$(METRICS)),--metrics $(if $(METRICS_BIND),--metrics-bind $(METRICS_BIND))) \
101:   $(if $(API_KEY),--api-key $(API_KEY)) \
102:   $(if $(EXPOSE),--expose $(EXPOSE)) \
103:   $(ARGS)
104: SERVER_ENV = $(if $(LOG_LEVEL),IGNIS_LOG_LEVEL=$(LOG_LEVEL)) $(if $(LOG_FORMAT),IGNIS_LOG_FORMAT=$(LOG_FORMAT))
105: SMOKE_MODEL := $(or $(MODEL),qwen3.8-27b)
106: # A generated key (API_KEY=auto) is unknown to make: pass the printed one.
107: SMOKE_AUTH := $(if $(filter-out auto,$(API_KEY)),-H 'Authorization: Bearer $(API_KEY)')
108: 
109: GPU_GUARDED := $(and $(filter 1,$(CUDA)),$(filter 1,$(GPU_CHECK)))
110: 
111: # $(call rfiles,<dir>): every file below <dir>, recursively (directories are
112: # descended, never listed: `<entry>/.` only exists for a directory).
113: rfiles = $(foreach e,$(wildcard $(1:=/*)),$(if $(wildcard $e/.),$(call rfiles,$e),$e))
114: 
115: # What the server binary is made of. Test trees are left out: they never
116: # reach the binary. web/dist is embedded by crates/server/build.rs. The
117: # kernel sources mirror the whitelist in crates/artifact/build.rs and only
118: # count for a CUDA build.
119: SERVER_CRATES := server core runtime artifact logging
120: SERVER_INPUTS := Cargo.toml $(wildcard .cargo/config.toml) \
121:   $(foreach c,$(SERVER_CRATES),crates/$c/Cargo.toml $(wildcard crates/$c/build.rs) $(call rfiles,crates/$c/src)) \
122:   $(call rfiles,web/dist)
123: ifeq ($(CUDA),1)
124:   SERVER_INPUTS += $(wildcard kernel/CMakeLists.txt) $(KERNEL_BUILD_INPUTS) \
125:     $(foreach r,src include vendor/src vendor/include,$(call rfiles,kernel/$r))
126: endif
127: 
128: WEB_INDEX := web/dist/index.html
129: WEB_DEPS := web/node_modules/.package-lock.json
130: WEB_INPUTS := $(call rfiles,web/src) \
131:   $(wildcard web/index.html web/package.json web/vite.config.ts web/tsconfig.json web/mock.ts)
132: 
133: # $(call stale_error,<what>,<file>,<newer inputs>,<fix>)
134: define stale_error
135: if [ -e "$2" ]; then \
136:   echo "error: $1 is out of date ($2)"; \
137:   echo "  changed since it was built:"; \
138:   for f in $(wordlist 1,8,$3); do echo "    $$f"; done; \
139:   $(if $(word 9,$3),echo "    ... and $(words $(wordlist 9,999999,$3)) more";) \
140: else \
141:   echo "error: $1 is not built ($2)"; \
142: fi; \
143: echo "  fix: $4"; \
144: exit 1
145: endef

191: .PHONY: doctor
192: doctor: ## Check the toolchain, the artifact and the web deps
193: 	@missing=0; \
194: 	check() { \
195: 	  if command -v "$$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '  ok       %s\n' "$$1"; \
196: 	  elif [ "$$2" = optional ]; then printf '  optional %s (%s)\n' "$$1" "$$3"; \
197: 	  else printf '  MISSING  %s (%s)\n' "$$1" "$$3"; missing=1; fi; \
198: 	}; \
199: 	echo "tools:"; \
200: 	check $(CARGO) required "https://rustup.rs"; \
201: 	check rustup required "https://rustup.rs"; \
202: 	check $(NPM) required "Node.js, for the Playground"; \
203: 	check curl required "smoke / status checks"; \
204: 	$(foreach t,$(OS_REQUIRED_TOOLS),check $(t) required "$(OS_TOOL_HINT)";) \
205: 	$(foreach t,$(OS_OPTIONAL_TOOLS),check $(t) optional "$(OS_TOOL_HINT)";) \
206: 	if $(CARGO) watch --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "  ok       cargo-watch"; \
207: 	else echo "  optional cargo-watch (make watch: cargo install cargo-watch)"; fi; \
208: 	echo "rust target:"; \
209: 	if rustup target list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "$(TARGET_TRIPLE)"; then echo "  ok       $(TARGET_TRIPLE)"; \
210: 	else echo "  MISSING  $(TARGET_TRIPLE) (make setup)"; missing=1; fi; \
211: 	echo "artifact:"; \
212: 	if [ -f "$(ARTIFACT)" ]; then echo "  ok       $(ARTIFACT)"; \
213: 	else echo "  missing  $(ARTIFACT) (only needed with CUDA=1)"; fi; \
214: 	echo "web:"; \
215: 	if [ -f "$(WEB_DEPS)" ]; then echo "  ok       web/node_modules"; \
216: 	else echo "  missing  web/node_modules (make web-install)"; fi; \
217: 	if [ -f "$(WEB_INDEX)" ]; then echo "  ok       web/dist"; \
218: 	else echo "  missing  web/dist (make web-build; UI=1 builds do it for you)"; fi; \
219: 	$(OS_DOCTOR) \
220: 	exit $$missing

222: .PHONY: setup
223: setup: web-install ## Install the Rust target and the web dependencies
224: 	rustup target add $(TARGET_TRIPLE)

226: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
227: ##@ Build
228: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
229: 
230: .PHONY: build
231: build: $(if $(filter 1,$(UI)),web-build) ## Build ignis-server (CUDA=1 builds the kernel leaf too)
232: 	$(CARGO) build $(SERVER_CARGO_FLAGS)
233: 	@printf '%s\n' "$(BACKEND)" > "$(SERVER_STAMP)"
234: 	@echo "built $(SERVER_BIN)  (backend=$(BACKEND), profile=$(PROFILE), ui=$(if $(wildcard $(WEB_INDEX)),embedded,absent))"
235: 
236: .PHONY: build-all
237: build-all: ## Build every workspace binary (server, bench, inspect, vendor)
238: 	$(CARGO) build --workspace $(CARGO_TARGET) --profile $(PROFILE) $(WORKSPACE_FEATURES)
239: 
240: .PHONY: kernel
241: kernel: ## Build the C++/CUDA kernel leaf only
242: 	$(KERNEL_BUILD)
243: 
244: .PHONY: release
245: release: ## Clean-slate release build: web + GPU server
246: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory web-build
247: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory build PROFILE=release CUDA=1 UI=1
248: 
249: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
250: ##@ Run
251: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
252: 
253: .PHONY: run
254: run: _require-built $(if $(GPU_GUARDED),gpu-guard) ## Run the last build in the foreground (never builds)
255: 	$(SERVER_ENV) $(SERVER_BIN) $(SERVER_FLAGS)
256: 
257: .PHONY: dev
258: dev: ## Build, then run in the foreground (stops at a build error)
259: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory build
260: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory run
261: 
262: .PHONY: mock
263: mock: ## `make dev` on the CPU mock: no GPU, no kernel leaf, no artifact
264: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory dev CUDA=0
265: 
266: .PHONY: start
267: start: _require-built $(if $(GPU_GUARDED),gpu-guard) ## Daemon: start in the background, outlives the terminal until make stop
268: 	@mkdir -p "$(RUNTIME_DIR)"
269: 	@$(SERVER_ENV) $(SERVER_START)
270: 
271: .PHONY: stop
272: stop: ## Stop the background server (FORCE=1 also stops one make did not start)
273: 	@$(SERVER_STOP)
274: 
275: .PHONY: restart
276: restart: ## Stop, then start the last build again (no build)
277: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory stop
278: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory start
279: 
280: .PHONY: redeploy
281: redeploy: ## Build, and only if it succeeds: stop + start
282: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory build
283: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory stop
284: 	$(MAKE) --no-print-directory start
285: 
286: .PHONY: status
287: status: ## Is the server up? (process, pid file, /v1/models)
288: 	-@$(SERVER_STATUS)
289: 	@code=$$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 2 "$(SERVER_URL)/v1/models" 2>/dev/null); \
290: 	case "$$code" in \
291: 	  200) echo "http: $(SERVER_URL) is serving";; \
292: 	  401) echo "http: $(SERVER_URL) is serving (API key required)";; \
293: 	  *) echo "http: nothing answering on $(SERVER_URL)";; \
294: 	esac
295: 
296: .PHONY: logs
297: logs: ## Follow the background server log
298: 	@[ -f "$(SERVER_LOG)" ] || { echo "no log at $(SERVER_LOG) (make start writes it)"; exit 1; }
299: 	tail -n 100 -f "$(SERVER_LOG)"

301: .PHONY: smoke
302: smoke: ## One /v1/models + one short chat completion against BIND
303: 	curl -fsS $(SMOKE_AUTH) "$(SERVER_URL)/v1/models"
304: 	@echo ""
305: 	curl -fsS $(SMOKE_AUTH) "$(SERVER_URL)/v1/chat/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
306: 	  -d '{"model":"$(SMOKE_MODEL)","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi in five words."}],"max_tokens":32}'
307: 	@echo ""
308: 
309: .PHONY: metrics
310: metrics: ## Scrape the metrics listener (a server started with METRICS=1; no key)
311: 	curl -fsS "$(METRICS_URL)/metrics"

313: .PHONY: canary
314: canary: ## ignis-bench canary suite against the running server
315: 	$(CARGO) run -p ignis-bench $(CARGO_TARGET) -- canary --endpoint $(SERVER_URL)

317: # Freshness guard for run/start: fails with the reason instead of building.
318: # The sub-make's own "*** Error" trailer is dropped; the reason is on stdout.
319: .PHONY: _require-built
320: _require-built:
321: 	@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory STRICT=1 _fresh 2>/dev/null || { echo "(run/start never build: see the fix above)"; exit 1; }

323: .PHONY: _fresh
324: _fresh: $(SERVER_BIN) $(if $(filter 1,$(UI)),$(if $(wildcard $(WEB_INDEX)),$(WEB_INDEX))) $(if $(filter 1,$(CUDA)),_require-artifact)

377: 	@$(CARGO) watch --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: cargo-watch not installed"; echo "  fix: cargo install cargo-watch"; exit 1; }

394: 	@touch "$@"

3: #   EXE                    executable suffix

7: #   KERNEL_BUILD_INPUTS    extra files whose change makes a CUDA server stale

9: #   GPU_GUARD              exit non-zero while the GPU is held

11: #   SERVER_START           start $(SERVER_BIN) in the background, wait for ready
12: #   SERVER_STOP            stop it (FORCE=1: any ignis-server)

32: # `powershell` to the SysWOW64 copy: a 32-bit PowerShell that cannot see

34: # hand the line to sh (64-bit), which starts the real 64-bit PowerShell. Since

1: // The chat request the Playground sends (GitHub #164): ignis's own
2: // `POST /v1/chat/completions`, streaming with the usage chunk, plus the
3: // thinking effort and the ignis lane tag extension `class`. With tools on,
4: // it also declares them, and the system message is the ignis prompt (what
5: // the tools add, read-only) followed by the owner's own.
6: 
7: import type { ToolCall } from "./sse.ts";
8: 
9: export type LaneTag = "interactive" | "agent";
10: 
11: /**
12:  * The efforts the loaded Qwen 3.8 template accepts (`high` is refused).
13:  * `none` turns thinking off, so the request never also sends
14:  * `enable_thinking` — ignis rejects the two when they disagree.
15:  */
16: export const REASONING_EFFORTS = ["none", "low", "medium", "xhigh"] as const;
17: export type ReasoningEffort = (typeof REASONING_EFFORTS)[number];
18: 
19: export type Settings = {
20:   model: string;
21:   systemPrompt: string;
22:   temperature: number;
23:   topP: number;
24:   /** `null` leaves the cap to the engine. */
25:   maxTokens: number | null;
26:   reasoningEffort: ReasoningEffort;
27:   laneTag: LaneTag;
28: };
29: 
30: /** A turn of the conversation: an assistant turn may call tools, a tool turn answers one call. */
31: export type Turn = { role: "user" | "assistant" | "tool"; content: string; toolCalls?: ToolCall[]; toolCallId?: string };
32: 
33: /** An OpenAI function tool, as `tools[]` declares it. */
34: export type ToolDefinition = {
35:   type: "function";
36:   function: { name: string; description: string; parameters: object };
37: };
38: 
39: type WireMessage = {
40:   role: "system" | "user" | "assistant" | "tool";
41:   content: string;
42:   tool_calls?: { id: string; type: "function"; function: { name: string; arguments: string } }[];
43:   tool_call_id?: string;
44: };
45: 
46: export type ChatRequest = {
47:   model: string;
48:   messages: WireMessage[];
49:   tools?: ToolDefinition[];
50:   stream: true;
51:   stream_options: { include_usage: true };
52:   temperature: number;
53:   top_p: number;
54:   max_tokens?: number;
55:   reasoning_effort: ReasoningEffort;
56:   class: LaneTag;
57: };
58: 
59: /** One message already in the Playground's conversation. */
60: export type Exchange = Turn & { failed: boolean };
61: 
62: /**
63:  * What of the conversation goes back to the engine: every exchange except
64:  * the ones that produced nothing — a prompt whose reply failed or came back
65:  * empty is dropped together with that reply, so the history never holds two
66:  * user turns in a row. A reply stopped part-way keeps the text it got.
67:  * Reasoning is never resent.
68:  */
69: export function conversationTurns(entries: Exchange[]): Turn[] {
70:   const turns: Turn[] = [];
71:   // A reply that only called tools is not empty: its calls are the turn.
72:   const empty = (e: Exchange | undefined) =>
73:     e !== undefined && e.role === "assistant" && (e.failed || (!e.content && !e.toolCalls?.length));
74:   for (let i = 0; i < entries.length; i++) {
75:     const entry = entries[i];
76:     if (entry.role === "user" && empty(entries[i + 1])) {
77:       i++;
78:       continue;
79:     }
80:     if (empty(entry)) continue;
81:     turns.push({
82:       role: entry.role,
83:       content: entry.content,
84:       ...(entry.toolCalls?.length ? { toolCalls: entry.toolCalls } : {}),
85:       ...(entry.toolCallId ? { toolCallId: entry.toolCallId } : {}),
86:     });
87:   }
88:   return turns;
89: }
90: 
91: function wireMessage(turn: Turn): WireMessage {
92:   return {
93:     role: turn.role,
94:     content: turn.content,
95:     ...(turn.toolCalls?.length
96:       ? {
97:           tool_calls: turn.toolCalls.map((c) => ({
98:             id: c.id,
99:             type: "function" as const,
100:             function: { name: c.name, arguments: c.arguments },
101:           })),
102:         }
103:       : {}),
104:     ...(turn.toolCallId ? { tool_call_id: turn.toolCallId } : {}),
105:   };
106: }
107: 
108: /** What the enabled tools add to a request: their prompt, ahead of the owner's, and their definitions. */
109: export type ToolExtras = { ignisPrompt?: string; tools?: ToolDefinition[] };
110: 
111: export function buildChatRequest(settings: Settings, turns: Turn[], extras: ToolExtras = {}): ChatRequest {
112:   const system = [extras.ignisPrompt ?? "", settings.systemPrompt].filter((part) => part.trim() !== "").join("\n\n");
113:   return {
114:     model: settings.model,
115:     messages: [...(system ? [{ role: "system" as const, content: system }] : []), ...turns.map(wireMessage)],
116:     ...(extras.tools?.length ? { tools: extras.tools } : {}),
117:     stream: true,
118:     stream_options: { include_usage: true },
119:     temperature: settings.temperature,
120:     top_p: settings.topP,
121:     ...(settings.maxTokens !== null ? { max_tokens: settings.maxTokens } : {}),
122:     reasoning_effort: settings.reasoningEffort,
123:     class: settings.laneTag,
124:   };
125: }

1: import { authHeaders } from "../api/auth.ts";
2: import { type Family, type ParseError, parseExposition } from "./exposition.ts";
3: import { append, HISTORY_MS, isRestart, type Point } from "./history.ts";
4: import { readSnapshot } from "./snapshot.ts";
5: 
6: // Scraping `GET /ui/metrics` from the browser (GitHub #165, ADR 0017): the
7: // Playground's copy of the exposition on the API listener, key-gated when
8: // ignis runs with --api-key. A 404 means metrics are off, a 401 that the key
9: // is missing or wrong. The state below is a pure reduction of scrape results
10: // so the cadence and the history are testable without a timer.
11: 
12: export type ScrapeResult =
13:   | { kind: "ok"; text: string }
14:   | { kind: "off" }
15:   | { kind: "unauthorized" }
16:   | { kind: "failed"; message: string };
17: 
18: /** `probing` until the first answer; `unreachable` when a scrape failed. */
19: export type Availability = "probing" | "on" | "off" | "unauthorized" | "unreachable";
20: 
21: export type MonitorState = {
22:   availability: Availability;
23:   /** Why the last scrape failed, when it did. */
24:   message: string | null;
25:   paused: boolean;
26:   intervalMs: number;
27:   points: Point[];
28:   last: { at: number; raw: string; scrapeMs: number; families: Family[]; errors: ParseError[] } | null;
29:   /** When a scrape found the counters gone down, inside the history. */
30:   restarts: number[];
31: };
32: 
33: /** The poll interval's range (2–5 s) and its default. */
34: const MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000;
35: const MAX_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;
36: /** How often to look again while metrics are off, locked or never reached. */
37: export const OFF_RETRY_MS = 30_000;
38: 
39: export function initialMonitor(): MonitorState {
40:   return {
41:     availability: "probing",
42:     message: null,
43:     paused: false,
44:     intervalMs: MAX_INTERVAL_MS,
45:     points: [],
46:     last: null,
47:     restarts: [],
48:   };
49: }
50: 
51: export function clampInterval(ms: number): number {
52:   return Math.min(MAX_INTERVAL_MS, Math.max(MIN_INTERVAL_MS, ms));
53: }
54: 
55: export async function fetchScrape(doFetch: typeof fetch = fetch): Promise<ScrapeResult> {
56:   try {
57:     const res = await doFetch("/ui/metrics", { headers: authHeaders(), cache: "no-store" });
58:     if (res.status === 404) return { kind: "off" };
59:     if (res.status === 401) return { kind: "unauthorized" };
60:     if (!res.ok) return { kind: "failed", message: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
61:     return { kind: "ok", text: await res.text() };
62:   } catch (err) {
63:     return { kind: "failed", message: String(err) };
64:   }
65: }
66: 
67: /** The state after a scrape that ended at `at` and took `scrapeMs`. */
68: export function applyScrape(state: MonitorState, result: ScrapeResult, at: number, scrapeMs: number): MonitorState {
69:   switch (result.kind) {
70:     case "off":
71:       return { ...state, availability: "off", message: null };
72:     case "unauthorized":
73:       return { ...state, availability: "unauthorized", message: null };
74:     case "failed":
75:       return { ...state, availability: "unreachable", message: result.message };
76:     case "ok": {
77:       const parsed = parseExposition(result.text);
78:       const snap = readSnapshot(parsed);
79:       const previous = state.points.at(-1);
80:       const points = append(state.points, { at, snap, scrapeMs }, HISTORY_MS);
81:       const from = points[0].at;
82:       const restarts = [...state.restarts, ...(previous && isRestart(previous.snap, snap) ? [at] : [])].filter((t) => t >= from);
83:       return {
84:         ...state,
85:         availability: "on",
86:         message: null,
87:         points,
88:         restarts,
89:         last: { at, raw: result.text, scrapeMs, families: [...parsed.families.values()], errors: parsed.errors },
90:       };
91:     }
92:   }
93: }
94: 
95: /** A server that answered before and has a history to show, even while a scrape fails. */
96: function hasLiveHistory(state: MonitorState): boolean {
97:   return state.availability === "on" || (state.availability === "unreachable" && state.points.length > 0);
98: }
99: 
100: /**
101:  * Whether the page offers the Monitor: metrics answered, or answered 401
102:  * (the Monitor says the key is wanted), or answered before and stopped.
103:  * A server without --metrics never shows it.
104:  */
105: export function monitorVisible(state: MonitorState): boolean {
106:   return hasLiveHistory(state) || state.availability === "unauthorized";
107: }
108: 
109: /** How long to wait before the next scrape. */
110: export function nextDelay(state: MonitorState): number {
111:   return hasLiveHistory(state) ? clampInterval(state.intervalMs) : OFF_RETRY_MS;
112: }

1: # Testing
2: 
3: How changes to this repo are verified. One rule governs everything
4: below: every code change ships with a test, and a task is not complete
5: until the test suite is green.
6: 
7: ## The gate
8: 
9: - `cargo test` from the workspace root — all five crates
10:   (`artifact`, `core`, `server`, `bench`, `vendor`).
11: - Machine-local smoke tests skip gracefully when their fixture is
12:   absent (e.g. `crates/artifact/tests/real_artifact.rs` needs the
13:   artifact in `F:\ai\q38`). A skip counts as green; a failure does not.
14: - **Exception — compute work: a skip is never green.** For anything on the
15:   forward pass (the kernel leaf, the step ABI, the program), a test that
16:   self-skips on a busy GPU or on a kernel error proves nothing; that pattern
17:   is what let a broken forward stay green for two tickets
18:   (`.scratch/REVIEW-2026-09-05.md` §4.1). Those tests belong to the explicit
19:   **GPU profile** (below), which requires the GPU free and *fails* on any
20:   kernel error, busy GPU, or missing fixture. The default `cargo test` stays
21:   CPU-only (GitHub #38).
22: - Kernel work (`kernel/`, CUDA) is not exercised by `cargo test`: build and
23:   run the leaf's own op-test executable (CTest) with `kernel/build.ps1 -Test`,
24:   and verify end to end through the GPU profile. The one kernel-adjacent thing
25:   `cargo test` *does* check is the vendored subtree's integrity
26:   (`crates/vendor`): a vendored file edited without a recorded patch turns the
27:   workspace red (ADR 0010, `kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md`).
28: - Playground work (`web/`, ADR 0026) is not exercised by `cargo test`
29:   either: its logic lives in pure modules with vitest tests, so a change
30:   there also needs `npm --prefix web test` and `npm --prefix web run build`
31:   (the typecheck) green — `make test-web web-build`. `cargo test` covers only the server's `/ui` routes.
32: - A `--features cuda` build rebuilds the leaf for you.
33:   `crates/artifact/build.rs` watches every file under `kernel/src`,
34:   `kernel/include`, `kernel/tests`, `kernel/vendor/src` and
35:   `kernel/vendor/include` (plus `CMakeLists.txt` and `build.ps1`) and runs
36:   `kernel/build.ps1` whenever one changes; a build with nothing to do costs
37:   a few seconds. Do not trust a binary built any other way to carry your
38:   kernel change: until GitHub #94 that script rebuilt only when
39:   `kernel/build/*.lib` was *missing*, so an edited `.cu` was linked from
40:   the previous archive with every test around it still green. That is what
41:   invalidated the first G2 gate run (#93).
42: 
43: ## The GPU test profile (ADR 0006, GitHub #38)
44: 
45: ignis and ninfer (the reference engine, also the coding agent's own model
46: runner) cannot share the RTX 5090 — a single engine's footprint already
47: takes ~28 GB of the 32 GB card (ADR 0006). So every GPU-touching Rust test
48: is `#[ignore]`d and runs only when asked for explicitly: `cargo test` never
49: touches the GPU on its own.
50: 
51: A GPU test decides what a busy GPU, a kernel error, or a missing fixture
52: means by asking [`ignis_core::gpu_profile`] — never by returning early on
53: its own:
54: 
55: - **Outside the profile** (`IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE` unset): those conditions
56:   print `SKIP: ...` and the test returns — a quick local check without
57:   stopping ninfer.
58: - **Under the profile** (`IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE=1`): the *same* conditions are
59:   hard failures (`panic!`), never a skip. This is the only mode whose green
60:   result counts for a gate.
61: 
62: Use it as `gpu_profile::check_rc(rc, "ignis_<op>")` for a kernel return
63: code, `check_compute_err(&e, "...")` for a `ComputeError`, and
64: `skip_or_fail("...")` for a missing fixture or an absent GPU. Its own unit
65: tests (in `crates/core/src/gpu_profile.rs`) pin the skip/fail decision on
66: CPU with an injected rc — no GPU needed, so they run in the default suite.
67: 
68: GPU-gated Rust tests use the `cuda` feature and `#[ignore]`: P1-21's
69: `gqa_layer_gpu` checks the BF16 exception and NVFP4 GQA layers against the
70: f64 oracle. They must use the helper above rather than reinventing a
71: self-skip. The GPU-side coverage also includes the kernel leaf's own op-test
72: executable (`kernel/build.ps1 -Test`), which the same runbook applies to.
73: 
74: ### Running the profile: `scripts/gpu-profile.ps1`
75: 
76: ADR 0006 calls the guard "a preflight check in the `bench`/test harness",
77: not a script a developer must remember to run standalone. So the profile
78: takes **two** things, not one: `IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE=1` *and* a preflight pass
79: on record. `scripts/gpu-preflight.ps1` writes a marker file
80: (`$env:TEMP\ignis-gpu-preflight.ok`) when it passes and clears it when it
81: refuses; `active()` reads that marker and **panics** if the variable is set
82: without a recent one. Setting the variable by hand therefore fails loudly
83: instead of running un-preflighted while ninfer may hold the card.
84: 
85: `crates/core` has no FFI and no GPU access of its own (GitHub #39 removed
86: the flat C-ABI surface), so the GPU is inspected by the script and the
87: verdict is carried across to Rust by that marker.
88: 
89: `scripts/gpu-profile.ps1` is the entry point that ties it together: it runs
90: the preflight, and only on a pass sets `IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE=1` and runs the
91: GPU-gated work. It consumes the marker — both it and
92: the env var are cleared before the script exits, pass or fail — so one
93: preflight authorizes exactly one run. A pass also ages out after 30 minutes,
94: which only matters if a run was killed before it could clean up.
95: **This script is the normal, documented way to run the GPU profile.**
96: 
97: It runs three stages and reports each one's wall time at the end, so a slow
98: run says where the time went without anyone adding up per-test output
99: (GitHub #135):
100: 
101: | Stage | What it runs | Parallelism |
102: |-------|--------------|-------------|
103: | `kernel/build.ps1 -Test` | the leaf's own op tests (CTest) | CTest's own |
104: | `cpu f64 layer oracle` | `layer_reference_real`, `--ignored` | libtest default |
105: | `gpu tests (serialized)` | everything else `--ignored` | `--test-threads=1` |
106: 
107: The middle stage exists because the f64 layer oracle touches no GPU: it
108: reads the stored weights through a memory map and evaluates them on the CPU.
109: It was paying for ADR 0006's exclusivity that it never needed, so it now
110: runs at full parallelism and the serialized stage skips it by name. It still
111: runs under `IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE=1`, so a missing artifact is a hard failure
112: there too.
113: 
114: **The test profile is optimized** (`[profile.dev]` and `[profile.test]`,
115: `opt-level = 2`). The f64 oracles are CPU-bound on scalar `f64` with
116: per-element NVFP4/W8 dequantization, and at the default `opt-level = 0` they
117: dominated the serialized stage. Rust applies no fast-math, so every `f64`
118: result and every measured tolerance is bit-identical to an unoptimized
119: build; `debug-assertions` and the overflow checks that follow them stay on.
120: The oracle also spreads its output rows over threads, which for the same
121: reason cannot move a bit: a row's sum is computed by the same code in the
122: same order whatever the split, pinned by a unit test that compares schedules
123: bit-for-bit and by `layer_reference_real` still matching the committed
124: fixtures, which were recorded by the scalar path.
125: 
126: **"Free" means one process on the card, not just "ninfer is stopped."** The
127: preflight inspects the GPU once, before the run starts; nothing stops a
128: second GPU-touching process from entering while the sweep is under way. One
129: clean profile run peaks at **26.1 GiB of the 5090's 32.6 GiB** (measured
130: 2026-09-13, sampled every 15s across two consecutive runs), so the headroom
131: left for anything else is about 6 GiB — less than one more artifact load. A
132: test binary that loses that race dies the way GitHub #145 recorded it: an
133: abrupt process exit, `exit code: 1`, no panic text and nothing printed
134: despite `--nocapture`, and the same test passing immediately when re-run
135: alone. Two unrelated tests died that way in one session, which is what a
136: contended card looks like from inside a test log — there is no diagnostic
137: that says so.
138: 
139: So before launching **any** GPU work — the profile, a bench run, a gate
140: leg, a single `--ignored` test — check that nobody has already launched
141: some. That includes another agent session in another worktree: the
142: worktrees are separate, the card is not. `nvidia-smi` (or
143: `scripts/gpu-preflight.ps1`) plus `tasklist` for stray `*_gpu-*.exe`,
144: `ignis-server`, `ignis-bench` and `ninfer*` processes answers it in one
145: step; `make gpu-status` prints both, and `make gpu-guard` turns them into a
146: pass/fail.
147: 
148: Runbook:
149: 
150: ```powershell
151: # 0. Check nobody else is already running GPU work -- another agent session
152: #    in another worktree counts. nvidia-smi for held memory, tasklist for
153: #    stray *_gpu-*.exe / ignis-server / ignis-bench / ninfer processes.
154: # 1. Stop ninfer (frees the VRAM the GPU profile needs).
155: # 2. Preflight + profile in one step: refuses to proceed while the GPU is
156: #    held (and names the offending process); on a free GPU, runs the leaf's
157: #    op tests and the #[ignore]d Rust GPU tests under IGNIS_GPU_PROFILE=1,
158: #    then clears it.
159: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gpu-profile.ps1
160: # -ThresholdMiB <n>    forwarded to gpu-preflight.ps1
161: # -SkipKernelBuild     Rust tests only, skip kernel/build.ps1 -Test
162: # -SkipCargoTests      kernel leaf only, skip both cargo stages
163: # 3. Restart ninfer.
164: ```
165: 
166: `make gpu-profile` runs the same script; `GPU_PROFILE_ARGS` forwards its
167: switches (`make gpu-profile GPU_PROFILE_ARGS=-SkipKernelBuild`).
168: 
169: `scripts/gpu-preflight.ps1` still exists as the standalone check
170: (`scripts/gpu-profile.ps1` calls it) for a quick "is the GPU free" query
171: that doesn't run anything.

283: #    artifact, then measure it on the same cells in the same session.

286:   --cells 8192,32768 --label ignis --profile "BF16 KV, 1024 chunk, eager" `

299: `ignis-server` takes the engine shape the run needs as flags (each over its

307: resident-token capacity that budget buys is derived from the format and

309: that event rather than computed from a flag.

403: ## The multimodal TTFT cell (GitHub #181)
404: 
405: `ignis-bench ttft --image <png>` adds one cell to a TTFT record: a fixed image
406: plus a short question (`--image-question`, default "Describe what this
407: screenshot shows in one sentence."), sent as content parts — the text first,
408: then the image as a `data:` URI. An error detector for the whole vision path,
409: not a gate. With `--image`, `--cells` may be omitted.
410: 
411: The committed image is `crates/bench/tests/fixtures/vision_ttft/screenshot.png`,
412: a 1280x800 editor screenshot drawn by `tools/vision-ttft/screenshot.py`
413: (deterministic; re-running it is a no-op). It sits on the 32-pixel grid, so it
414: expands to 1,000 vision tokens and the cell is 1,027 tokens with the default
415: question — `crates/bench/tests/ttft_image_real_frontend.rs` pins that against
416: the real frontend, and the reference counts it the same.

418: Cold in everything, like a text cell: each prompt (the warmup's too) starts
419: with its own nonce, and its image is the fixture with the top-left pixel
420: changed, so neither a prefix cache nor either engine's digest-keyed
421: preprocessing cache can serve it; the size, and so the length, is unchanged.
422: The record names the image (SHA-256, size, question), and `g2` refuses to pair
423: cells of one length over different images, or an image cell with a text cell.
424: 
425: A record carrying the image cell cannot be compared with one that has none, so
426: the image cell is measured as its own record. The session is
427: `scripts/vision-ttft-session.sh <out-dir>`, run from the repository root on a
428: free card after a release build: the reference with `--vision` (the owner's
429: hq-e8-2b-262k preset), ignis with `--vision`, and ignis without it, **each
430: launched twice** (ADR 0021). Every launch writes a text record (1024, 8192 and
431: 32768 tokens, cut from the ninfer corpus) and, with vision, an image record;
432: `scripts/ttft-pool.py` pools each engine's two launches into one record, and
433: `g2` compares the pooled records: image against image, text against text, and
434: ignis's text with `--vision` against without. The 1.5 threshold `g2` prints is
435: G2's own; for this cell the ratios are error detectors.
436:

438: changed pixels — so a second `ttft` run against a live engine is served from
439: its prefix and media caches, and ignis reports no cached tokens for the void
440: rule to catch it. Restart the engine instead.

443: DFlash2 take ~29.8 GiB of their own (the retained pool is derived from what is
444: free after load), so the desktop's own VRAM decides whether the card
445: oversubscribes; when it does, every cell comes back slower and erratic rather
446: than failing. The script samples `nvidia-smi` beside every launch — distrust
447: one whose peak reaches the total

450: ## The KV-format A/B: 2x2 over engine and format (GitHub #139)
451: 
452: What it answers: how much the hq-e8-2b KV format costs against BF16, whether
453: that cost is ours or the format's, and what the card is actually doing while it
454: is paid. The result of the 2026-09-13 run is

459: capacity*. A BF16 token costs 65,536 bytes against hq-e8-2b's 9,216 (7.11x, see

461: same byte budget buys 7.11x more pages under hq and a "just change the format"
462: run confounds the format with its page count. 65,536 tokens is the value to
463: pick: it is 1,024 pages, the geometry spec 03's ITL table and #114's cap
464: arithmetic assume, and the ITL fixture's peak of 65,344 tokens fits it with 192
465: to spare. Under hq that means asking for the smaller pool explicitly
466: (`--kv-pool-bytes 576M`), because its default 4 GiB buys 465,984 tokens.

535: 
536: Every `ignis-bench` subcommand drives its endpoint through one
537: `HttpEndpoint`, which sets an **explicit** per-request deadline: 1800 s by
538: default, and `IGNIS_BENCH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=<seconds>` overrides it (`0`
539: removes it entirely). Each run prints the deadline it is using on stderr
540: before its first request.
541: 
542: This is not a knob a normal run needs — it exists because the *implicit*
543: one cost a gate session. `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` carries an
544: undeclared 30-second total timeout that covers reading the response body,
545: so a streamed measurement request lives entirely inside it. The G4 needle
546: cell at 131,072 tokens (~30 s of prefill on this hardware) died on it
547: against **both** engines, every attempt, reporting `read SSE: error
548: decoding response body` — which reads like an engine fault and was chased
549: as one across four launches. The 65,536-token cell, at ~15 s, passed every
550: time.
551: 
552: Two consequences for anyone measuring here: the deadline is now the
553: harness's own declared number rather than a library default, and a request
554: that does hit it says so by name instead of surfacing as a decode error.
555: Raise it (or set `0`) for a cell whose legitimate wall time could approach
556: half an hour; never lower it to "make a run finish".

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live **exclusively on GitHub** (`gpillon/ignis`, via the `gh` CLI).
GitHub is the single source of truth for issue tracking: status, blocking
relationships, labels, and closure. Each GitHub issue body is short
(1-3 lines of context) and links to the implementation spec.

Implementation specs (acceptance criteria, seam description, ADR references)
live under `.scratch/<feature>/specs/` in this repo. These are **specs, not
issues** — they do not track status or blocking (that is GitHub's job).
`.scratch/` is also used for temporary artifacts, experiments, and workflow
output, but **never for issue tracking**.

See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for the full convention.

### Triage labels

The five canonical triage roles, mapped 1:1 to same-name labels
(`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`).
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context — root `CONTEXT.md` for the glossary, `docs/adr/` for ADRs.
See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Findings

When recording or consulting durable findings from discovery, research, or
experiments, start from `docs/findings/README.md`.

### Testing

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

### Make

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal
until Ctrl+C. `run` and `start` only ever launch the last build: a stale
binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

### Worktrees

All git worktrees for this repo live under `../.inference-qwen-worktrees/`
(sibling of the repo root), one subdirectory per issue/feature. Do not create
worktrees anywhere else (e.g. no separate `.inference-claude-worktrees/`) —
one shared location for every agent.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then

binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

1: # ignis kernel leaf: C++/CUDA static libraries behind a flat C ABI (ADR 0001),
2: # built on a vendored subtree of the reference's core and ops (ADR 0010).
3: # See kernel/NOTICE and kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md for provenance.
4: #
5: # Configure/build: kernel/build.ps1 (plain PowerShell, imports the MSVC env
6: # itself — same pattern as ninfer's configure-ninja.ps1/build-ninja.ps1).
7: # Run the leaf's own tests: kernel/build.ps1 -Test (or ctest from the build
8: # directory).
9: 
10: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
11: project(ignis-kernel LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)
12: 
13: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
15: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)
16: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
17: 
18: # RTX 5090 (Blackwell consumer). Proven on this machine with CMake 3.28
19: # (NINFER_WINDOWS_BUILD_NOTES section 14).
20: if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)
21:   set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 120a)
22: endif()
23: 
24: # -GS- : the kernel objects are linked into a Rust binary via lld, which cannot
25: # satisfy the /GS security-cookie symbols (__security_cookie,
26: # __security_check_cookie, __GSHandlerCheck) that MSVC emits by default. /GS is
27: # irrelevant for compute kernels (no stack-buffer semantics), so disable it —
28: # for the C++ translation units of the vendored core as well as for CUDA. The
29: # final Rust link provides the MSVC CRT (build.rs).
30: set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler -GS-")
31: set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} /GS-")
32: 
33: # CUDA::cudart (P1-07, GitHub #43; also needed by P1-08, GitHub #44; also
34: # needed by the P1-10/#46 bf16/w8 dispatch below, and by P1-16/#52's
35: # paged_kv_cache/linear_attention_state, which pull cudaStream_t in through
36: # core/device.h): the vendored op wrappers' public headers declare
37: # host-callable functions taking a `cudaStream_t`, and the op-test harness
38: # calls the CUDA runtime API (cudaMemcpyAsync, stream sync) directly from
39: # plain .cpp translation units — unlike the .cu sources, MSVC's cl.exe does
40: # not see the CUDA toolkit's include/lib dirs on its own for those.
41: find_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)
42: 
43: # --- the vendored reference substrate (ADR 0010, GitHub #42, #43, #44, #46, #52) -
44: #
45: # Verbatim copies of the reference's core, ops-common headers and (from P1-07)
46: # the norm/glue op families, pinned by kernel/vendor/manifest.json and
47: # maintained by scripts/vendor-ninfer.ps1. Vendored files keep the reference's
48: # include paths (`core/...`, `ops/common/...`, `ops/kernel/...`,
49: # `ops/launcher/...`), so `kernel/vendor/src` is the include root and a diff
50: # against the source stays trivial. Public op headers keep the reference's
51: # `ninfer/ops/...` include path, rooted at `kernel/vendor/include`.
52: #
53: # The source list is explicit, not a glob: the manifest is the only thing that
54: # decides what is vendored, and a glob would silently absorb a stray file.

experiments, start from `docs/findings/README.md`.

Every code change ships with a test, and the task is not complete until
`cargo test` passes workspace-wide. Before launching **anything** on the GPU
(the profile, a bench run, a gate leg, one `--ignored` test), always check
that no other test, bench or agent session is already using the card — in
any worktree. The 5090 fits one run at a time and the loser dies with no
diagnostic. See `docs/agents/testing.md`.

`make help` lists the targets; `make config` prints the exact server command
a run will use. An agent runs the server as a daemon — `make start`, then
`make stop` — since `run`, `dev`, `dev-ui` and `watch` hold the terminal

binary fails naming the changed files, and `make build` is the fix.
`make gpu-status` is the one-command check before GPU work. Why it is
shaped this way: ADR 0027.

1: # ignis kernel leaf: C++/CUDA static libraries behind a flat C ABI (ADR 0001),
2: # built on a vendored subtree of the reference's core and ops (ADR 0010).
3: # See kernel/NOTICE and kernel/vendor/VENDOR.md for provenance.
4: #
5: # Configure/build: kernel/build.ps1 (plain PowerShell, imports the MSVC env
6: # itself — same pattern as ninfer's configure-ninja.ps1/build-ninja.ps1).
7: # Run the leaf's own tests: kernel/build.ps1 -Test (or ctest from the build
8: # directory).
9: 
10: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)
11: project(ignis-kernel LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)
12: 
13: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
14: set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
15: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)
16: set(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
17: 
18: # RTX 5090 (Blackwell consumer). Proven on this machine with CMake 3.28
19: # (NINFER_WINDOWS_BUILD_NOTES section 14).
20: if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)
21:   set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 120a)
22: endif()
23: 
24: # -GS- : the kernel objects are linked into a Rust binary via lld, which cannot
25: # satisfy the /GS security-cookie symbols (__security_cookie,
26: # __security_check_cookie, __GSHandlerCheck) that MSVC emits by default. /GS is
27: # irrelevant for compute kernels (no stack-buffer semantics), so disable it —
28: # for the C++ translation units of the vendored core as well as for CUDA. The
29: # final Rust link provides the MSVC CRT (build.rs).
30: set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler -GS-")
31: set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} /GS-")
32: 
33: # CUDA::cudart (P1-07, GitHub #43; also needed by P1-08, GitHub #44; also
34: # needed by the P1-10/#46 bf16/w8 dispatch below, and by P1-16/#52's
35: # paged_kv_cache/linear_attention_state, which pull cudaStream_t in through
36: # core/device.h): the vendored op wrappers' public headers declare
37: # host-callable functions taking a `cudaStream_t`, and the op-test harness
38: # calls the CUDA runtime API (cudaMemcpyAsync, stream sync) directly from
39: # plain .cpp translation units — unlike the .cu sources, MSVC's cl.exe does
40: # not see the CUDA toolkit's include/lib dirs on its own for those.
41: find_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)
42: 
43: # --- the vendored reference substrate (ADR 0010, GitHub #42, #43, #44, #46, #52) -
44: #
45: # Verbatim copies of the reference's core, ops-common headers and (from P1-07)
46: # the norm/glue op families, pinned by kernel/vendor/manifest.json and
47: # maintained by scripts/vendor-ninfer.ps1. Vendored files keep the reference's
48: # include paths (`core/...`, `ops/common/...`, `ops/kernel/...`,
49: # `ops/launcher/...`), so `kernel/vendor/src` is the include root and a diff
50: # against the source stays trivial. Public op headers keep the reference's
51: # `ninfer/ops/...` include path, rooted at `kernel/vendor/include`.
52: #
53: # The source list is explicit, not a glob: the manifest is the only thing that
54: # decides what is vendored, and a glob would silently absorb a stray file.
55: set(IGNIS_VENDOR_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/vendor)
